title: HostId
description: The one declaration of harness host identity (#446). Every host-bearing schema references this file instead of carrying its own enum. `scripts/host_identity.py` owns the same identity set and the same external-id pattern, and `tests/test_host_identity.py` pins the two together, so the rule has one source and one proof. A *built-in* host is one of the six pstack ships native drivers, projections and receipts for. A *declared* host is namespaced (`acme:copilot`): it may be described by a local adapter profile, but it starts at candidate with unproved bindings and its receipt must name the adapter_version it was produced by.

known.description: The six built-in hosts plus the two pre-registry names existing profiles and receipts still carry (`claude`, `custom`).

observer.description: A host a receipt may name for an observation that is not a real harness.

external.description: A declared external host id: `<namespace>:<name>`, two lowercase labels. A bare new name is refused because it would collide with the flat built-in namespace, and no dot, slash, underscore or uppercase may appear, so an id can never be read as a path or a host name to probe.

host.description: An identity a profile, binding or package descriptor may carry: a built-in host or a declared namespaced one.

receiptHost.description: An identity a verification receipt may carry: the profile set plus the observer host.
